long_biography.plain_text:
Lee entered the cattle industry as a jackeroo and bought his first property in 1968. The launch platform was not entirely independent. His father, Norman, had built and sold an earthmoving business before acquiring Brindley Park, where the younger Lee developed cattle operations and early commercial feedlots.

The business that became Australian Country Choice grew around a long supply relationship with Coles. It integrated breeding properties, backgrounding, feedlots, processing, retail packing and distribution rather than relying on one stage of the beef market. Lee now serves as principal and director, while his son Anthony leads the business as chief executive. ACC remains family-owned, so its land, livestock and plants should be understood as company assets rather than as a list of Trevor Lee's personally titled property.

uncertainties.detail: Trevor Lee is a common name. The accepted match is the Australian Country Choice founder because the owner metadata identifies an Australian man resident and born in Australia, and focused wealth searches consistently surface the Australian cattle-business owner. No employer or company anchor is stored in the source record, so identity confidence remains below very high.

The source record's portrait appears to depict Trevor Lee Caddell, the American professional wrestler known as Trevor Lee and Cameron Grimes. Sports Illustrated establishes that namesake as American and North Carolina-based, conflicting with the owner record's Australian metadata. No wrestler biography, dates or social profiles are imported.

Two Dun & Bradstreet company profiles connect the full name Trevor James Lee to ACC and Lee Group entities at the Cannon Hill address. James is proposed at high rather than very-high confidence because the supporting corporate profiles are third-party compilations rather than direct registry extracts.

ACC is described as family-owned, and independent reporting identifies Trevor Lee as owner. Public sources do not publish his exact individual percentage across every entity. Cattle stations, livestock, feedlots, processing plants, aircraft, charter operations and property are therefore treated as company or group assets, not automatically as personally titled holdings.

Some media call Lee self-made, while the fuller history shows a substantial platform from his father's earlier business success and Brindley Park acquisition. Self-made — advantaged start preserves Lee's founder-built expansion without overlooking that platform; no inherited controlling stake is established.

The source record states Australia as birth country, but no reliable public source located establishes Lee's exact birth day, month, year or city. The interview chronology supports only an approximate age and is not converted into a birth-year proposal.
No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was verified. The canonical ACC company website is proposed. No dedicated Forbes profile was found; namesake coverage was rejected.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, irrelevant private-family detail, personal-net-worth estimates and vessel research are excluded. Family details are limited to the business starting platform and current succession needed to explain wealth origin and control.
